# Tanager pilot review — Ferndale depot, weeks three and four

2026-06-16, 13:30 to 14:50, in the crew room at Ferndale with the yard door open the whole time. Typed as we went, so the quotes are close but not exact.

In the room: Marta Kubik (field operations), Cal Merrick (crew lead, Ferndale), Oliver Renn (me). On the call: Deshawn Pryor (Harrow integrations) and Fiona Aitken (Quillon Systems).

Four weeks in. Eleven techs on the app, nobody has dropped off it, and Cal has quietly stopped printing the morning sheet, which he had not mentioned to anyone until I asked what the printer was doing switched off.

Cal on the handsets: no complaints worth writing down. Two cracked screens, both cracked before the app went on. Battery is the one real thing — a day with a lot of photos takes a phone to about 15% by four o'clock, and the vans have chargers but most of the leads have walked.

Marta cut that off before it could turn into a procurement conversation. "We are not buying tablets. That was settled in March and it stays settled. Tanager runs on the phones the crews already have."

Then the thing that took most of the hour. Cal's crews keep finding jobs they closed on the app the night before still sitting open in Harrow the next morning. Not every night, and always the late ones.

Deshawn had the answer ready and was slightly irritated nobody had asked him sooner. Harrow does not take writes between one and four in the morning. It is shut in that window while the overnight run rebuilds the day, it has been shut in that window since it went in, and anything Tanager pushes into it queues and lands at four. What Cal is looking at is a leak job closed at 01:20 sitting in a queue for two hours and forty minutes.

Cal: "So it is not lost."

Deshawn: "It has never been lost. It is just not there yet."

Fiona confirmed the queue is on Quillon's side and drains at four whether anyone is watching it or not. She was careful to say this is not the retry path — a retry is what happens on a 503, and Harrow does not return a 503, it accepts the connection and holds it. Marta's question was why a crew is closing a job at half one at all. Cal said leak jobs run late and always have, and that if we want them closed before one we should say so and staff it.

Marta then asked the question she came in with. Before Skelby goes anywhere: who is building the day's run after the pilot?

Fiona took that as an opening and pitched Quillon's routing module. It sequences on drive time, it re-optimises when a job overruns, and it is a separate licence that nobody at Ashgrove has bought or costed. She was straight that she was pitching and said so twice.

Deshawn was not keen and did not dress it up. "I want a long look at that before anybody says yes. What I do not want is two systems both deciding what a crew does at nine in the morning."

Nobody settled it. Marta wants an answer before the Skelby scope goes to the sponsor, and the people who would have to give her one — network planning — have not sat in a Tanager meeting since March.

The paper book came up last, from Fiona, who suggested Skelby cut over without it and let Ferndale keep it for the rest of the pilot. Her argument was the one she made in May: a crew carrying both will trust the paper, and the pilot will end up measuring the paper.

Marta was short with it. "The book stays in the van until we close the pilot. Nobody is binning it in week three."

Cal backed her, on hydrants. Nine hydrant jobs since cutover and every one of them went in the book, because there is no asset for a hydrant and so nothing to open on the phone. Fiona said that is a data question rather than an app question and it is not on the pilot's list. Nobody argued with her and nobody wrote it down anywhere it would be picked up.

Marta still has not set a date the pilot formally closes. She acknowledged that is the thing the book question hangs on and has been since May.

Open at the end:

- Deshawn to get network planning into a room before the Skelby scope goes up
- Cal to chase the van charger leads through facilities, which he was clear is not a Tanager problem and should not be counted as one
- the pilot close date, still with Marta, second time of asking
